title: Nephi addresses Joseph
summary: Nephi addresses Joseph, recalls Joseph's birth in the wilderness and bringing him out of it, and speaks of an inheritance in the land, the Lord's blessing, and Joseph's seed.

explicit_facts.text: Nephi addresses Joseph as his last-born.
Joseph's mother bore him in the wilderness during Nephi's days of greatest sorrow.
Nephi speaks of the land as an inheritance for Joseph and his seed with his brethren, conditional on keeping the commandments of the Holy One of Israel.
Nephi says he brought Joseph out of the wilderness of his afflictions and says Joseph's seed shall not utterly be destroyed.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Joseph can be shown listening while Nephi addresses him.
unspecified_visual_details: The location of the address is not stated.
Nephi's and Joseph's appearances are not stated.

spoken_dialogue.text: And now I speak unto you, Joseph, my last-born.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Nephi

spoken_dialogue.text: And may the Lord consecrate also unto thee this land,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Nephi

spoken_dialogue.text: if it so be that ye shall keep the commandments of the Holy One of Israel.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Nephi

spoken_dialogue.text: may the Lord bless thee forever, for thy seed shall not utterly be destroyed.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Nephi

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Joseph's birth and the journey out of the wilderness are recalled, not occurring during this address.
The Lord's blessing and the future of Joseph's seed are spoken of, not shown as visible events.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Joseph's birth or the wilderness journey as happening during this address.
Do not depict a divine appearance; none is described.
Do not add a speaker or dialogue not supplied in the verses.

title: Joseph’s lineage and covenant
summary: Lehi tells his son Joseph that he descends from Joseph who was carried captive into Egypt. He recounts the Lord’s covenants with that Joseph and the promise of a righteous branch from his lineage.

explicit_facts.text: Lehi says his son is the fruit of his loins and that he himself descends from Joseph who was carried captive into Egypt.
The Lord made covenants with Joseph who was carried captive into Egypt.
Lehi says that Joseph saw their day and received a promise that the Lord would raise up a righteous branch from his lineage.
The branch would be remembered in the Lord’s covenants, and the Messiah would be made manifest to them in the latter days.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Lehi speaks to his son Joseph.
unspecified_visual_details: The setting and the appearances of Lehi and his son are unstated.

spoken_dialogue.text: For behold, thou art the fruit of my loins; and I am a descendant of Joseph who was carried captive into Egypt.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Lehi

spoken_dialogue.text: Wherefore, Joseph truly saw our day.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Lehi

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Joseph’s vision, the promised branch, and the latter-day manifestation of the Messiah are recounted as prophecy, not as events occurring during this conversation.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Joseph in Egypt, the branch, or the Messiah as physically present.
Do not combine separate verse excerpts into a new quotation.

title: Joseph’s testimony recounted
summary: Lehi recounts Joseph’s testimony that the Lord would raise up a choice seer from Joseph’s descendants, commanding him to do work that would bring his brethren knowledge of the covenants.
characters: the Lord (quoted within Joseph’s reported testimony)

explicit_facts.text: The recounted testimony says the Lord would raise up a choice seer from Joseph’s descendants.

Joseph’s reported quotation of the Lord says the seer would be highly esteemed among Joseph’s descendants and commanded to perform work of great worth, bringing his brethren knowledge of the covenants made with their fathers.
The Lord’s reported words restrict the seer to the commanded work and promise to make him great in the Lord’s eyes.

unspecified_visual_details: The setting, physical appearances, clothing, gestures, and staging are not specified.

spoken_dialogue.text: For Joseph truly testified, saying: A seer shall the Lord my God raise up, who shall be a choice seer unto the fruit of my loins.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Lehi (recounting Joseph’s testimony)

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Preserve the reporting layers: Lehi recounts Joseph’s testimony, which includes Joseph’s quotation of the Lord.
The seer’s work is foretold, not narrated as occurring.
References to descendants, brethren, and fathers do not establish their physical presence.
prohibited_inventions: Do not stage Joseph’s earlier testimony or the Lord’s reported speech as a new present-tense encounter.
Do not depict a visible divine appearance.
Do not show the foretold seer performing his work or supply his name.
Do not invent listeners, actions, or additional dialogue.

title: The seer and Moses
summary: Lehi's quoted prophecy compares the future seer to Moses and foretells Moses delivering the people from Egypt and the seer bringing forth and confirming the Lord's word.

explicit_facts.text: The seer would be great like Moses, whom the Lord would raise up to deliver Israel.
Moses would be raised up to deliver the people from Egypt.
A seer from Joseph's descendants would have power to bring forth the Lord's word and convince them of the word already gone forth among them.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Lehi continues delivering prophetic teaching to Joseph.
unspecified_visual_details: No appearance is described for Moses or the future seer.

narration.text: And he shall be great like unto Moses,
Moses will I raise up, to deliver thy people out of the land of Egypt.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The future deliverance and seer's work are prophecy, not present action.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Moses, Egypt, or the seer as present in the scene.

title: Writings Shall Grow Together
summary: The prophecy declares that descendants of the addressee and of Judah shall write, their writings shall grow together, and an unnamed man shall be made strong when the Lord’s work commences among his people.
characters: Joseph (prophecy attribution; not established as physically present)

explicit_facts.text: Descendants of the addressee and descendants of Judah shall write, and their writings shall grow together.

These writings shall confound false doctrines, lay down contentions, establish peace among the addressee’s descendants, and bring them to knowledge of their fathers and the Lord’s covenants in the latter days.
An unnamed male shall be made strong out of weakness when the Lord’s work commences among all his people, unto the restoration of the house of Israel.
Both declarations attribute their words to the Lord.

unspecified_visual_details: No physical setting, appearance, clothing, writing materials, or staging is specified.
The verses do not describe a visible appearance of Joseph, the Lord, the future writers, or the unnamed male.

spoken_dialogue.text: Wherefore, the fruit of thy loins shall write;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Joseph

spoken_dialogue.text: And out of weakness he shall be made strong, in that day when my work shall commence among all my people, unto the restoring thee, O house of Israel, saith the Lord.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Joseph

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Joseph is the prophecy’s speaker label supplied by the audit context; these two verses themselves attribute the declarations to the Lord.
The Lord is referenced as the authority for the words, not depicted as physically present or speaking directly in a newly staged encounter.
These are future prophetic declarations, not events occurring in the scene.
The writings growing together must not be rendered as a literal supernatural occurrence.
prohibited_inventions: Do not stage the future writing, strengthening, peace, or restoration as present events.
Do not invent a visible appearance or physical presence for Joseph or the Lord.
Do not identify the addressee or unnamed male beyond what these verses supply.
Do not invent particular books, writing materials, descendants, locations, or encounters.
Do not add dialogue or dramatize separate future times as one event.

title: Joseph's confidence in the promise
summary: Lehi quotes Joseph's confidence that the seer will be blessed, bear a name connected to Joseph and his father, and help bring his people to salvation; the Lord will preserve Joseph's seed.

explicit_facts.text: Joseph prophesied that the Lord would bless the seer and confound those who seek to destroy him.
The seer would be named after Joseph and after his father, and the Lord would bring his people to salvation by the seer's hand.
Joseph expressed confidence in the promise of Moses and said the Lord would preserve his seed forever.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Lehi recounts Joseph's words while speaking to his son.
unspecified_visual_details: The seer, his father, and the threatened opponents are not visually described.

narration.text: Behold, I am sure of the fulfilling of this promise;
I will preserve thy seed forever.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The seer's future danger and salvation are prophetic, not present events.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict an attack on the seer or a visible divine intervention.

title: Moses and a spokesman
summary: Lehi recounts the Lord's words concerning Moses receiving power in a rod and law in writing, with a spokesman, and a future descendant who writes with a spokesman to declare it.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord would raise up Moses, give him power in a rod and judgment in writing, and write his law by his own hand; Moses would have a spokesman.
The Lord would raise up one from Joseph's descendants, provide him a spokesman, and have him write the writing of Joseph's descendants for them to receive.
The spokesman of that descendant would declare the writing.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Lehi recounts the prophecy as teaching, without staging its future events.
unspecified_visual_details: The descendant, both spokesmen, the rod, and the writing are not visually described in this present scene.

narration.text: I will make a spokesman for him.
the spokesman of thy loins shall declare it.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: These are prophetic statements rather than present-tense visible events.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the Lord's hand writing or invent the identities or appearances of either spokesman.

title: Words from the dust
summary: Lehi recounts the prophecy that the descendants' written words will reach their brethren after generations and call them to repentance; the Lord will strengthen their words through faith.

explicit_facts.text: The writing would contain words the Lord deemed expedient to go forth to Joseph's descendants and be as though they cried to them from the dust.
After many generations, their cry would go to their brethren, including a call to repentance, in the simpleness of their words.
Because of their faith, their words would proceed from the Lord and be made strong, leading to remembrance of the covenant.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Lehi continues teaching Joseph about the future written words.
unspecified_visual_details: The generations, written words, and dust are not described as a literal visible scene.

narration.text: And it shall be as if the fruit of thy loins had cried unto them from the dust;

doctrinal_or_story_notes: “Cried unto them from the dust” is figurative teaching about written words, not a literal appearance or voice from the dead.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the dead speaking or a supernatural voice rising from dust.

title: Lehi applies the prophecy to Joseph
summary: Lehi tells Joseph that his father of old prophesied in this manner and blesses him under the covenant, saying his seed will not be destroyed because they will heed the book's words.

explicit_facts.text: Lehi tells Joseph that his father of old prophesied in this manner.
Lehi says Joseph is blessed because of the covenant and his seed will not be destroyed, for they will hearken to the words of the book.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Lehi directly addresses Joseph in applying the prophecy to him.
unspecified_visual_details: The book and the setting of the conversation are not described.

explicit_facts.text: One mighty would rise among Joseph's descendants and do much good in word and deed as an instrument in God's hands, with exceeding faith.
He would work mighty wonders and bring much restoration to the house of Israel and the seed of Joseph's brethren.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Lehi presents this as a prophecy to Joseph.

title: Lehi's final counsel to Joseph
summary: Lehi blesses Joseph, calls him little, counsels him to heed Nephi's words and remember his dying father, and concludes.

explicit_facts.text: Lehi blesses Joseph and says he is little.
Lehi tells Joseph to hearken to Nephi's words and remember his dying father.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Lehi speaks a closing blessing and counsel directly to Joseph.
